title: f(x) = x² − 3x and its gradient 2x − 3
caption: From first principles f′(x) = 2x − 3. The graph shows it: f has a flat bottom at x = 1.5, where 2x − 3 = 0; to the left f falls (negative gradient) and to the right it rises (positive gradient), with slope 3 at x = 3.
alt: The parabola y = x² − 3x with its minimum at x = 1.5 and the straight line y = 2x − 3, which is zero at x = 1.5.
description: Dividing the change in f by h and letting h → 0 gives f′(x) = 2x − 3.
The parabola f has its minimum at x = 1.5.
The gradient line crosses zero at the same place.
Where f is steepest on the right, at x = 3, the gradient line reads 3.

checks.name: the slope of f at x = -1 is 2x − 3 = −5
the slope of f at x = 0 is 2x − 3 = −3
the slope of f at x = 1.5 is 2x − 3 = 0
the slope of f at x = 3 is 2x − 3 = 3
